title: Professor Green Shares Hospital Visit of Son Amid Emotional Reveal on Celebs Go Dating
text:
The rapper Stephen Manderson, known as Professor Green, posted on Instagram that his five‑year‑old son Slimane lost a tooth and fractured his wrist during a holiday, prompting a hospital trip. The incident followed a tearful interview on Celebs Go Dating where Green opened up about grieving his split from ex‑partner Karima McAdams and the complexities of co‑parenting. The public discussion highlights male emotional vulnerability and the challenges of single‑parenting after a high‑profile breakup.
Professor Green , the British rapper whose real name is Stephen Manderson, disclosed a series of mishaps that left his five‑year‑old son Slimane in hospital during a family holiday.
The incidents unfolded on Wednesday when the boy lost his front tooth while enthusiastically greeting relatives, an episode that was captured in an Instagram Story posted by his mother, actress Karima McAdams. Karima, who shared a cheerful family photo with her eyes obscured by the rapper, wrote that Slimane's tooth was knocked out after he tried to kiss everyone and was head‑butted.
The following morning, the toddler suffered a suspected wrist fracture after falling off a zip‑wire, prompting an urgent visit to the A+E department. In a second Instagram update, Professor Green showed Slimane seated on an examination couch, his left arm encased in a plaster cast and wrapped in a blanket, joking about the string of misfortunes with a caption that read, "First tooth lost, first arm fractured... happy holidays.
" He also remarked on the condition of Slimane's white socks, calling them "state of his socks" in a light‑hearted tone. The hospital episode arrived on the heels of a profoundly emotional appearance by the rapper on the reality series Celebs Go Dating, where he openly discussed the lingering grief over his recent split from Karima.
During a feedback session with relationship coaches Anna Williamson and Dr Tara Suwinyattichaiporn, the 42‑year‑old reflected on the pain of co‑parenting after a five‑year relationship that began in 2019, an engagement in late 2021, and a breakup announced in April 2024. He described how the image of his envisioned family haunts him, saying, "I have a photograph in my head of what my son's family was going to look like. That was my family too. That's so tough.
" When asked about his emotional state, Green admitted to feeling complex and vulnerable, noting that men rarely discuss the emotional toll of separation, especially when children are involved. He emphasized his commitment to shielding Slimane from his own sorrow, stating, "I can't show him how upset I am all the time. I want to prioritise the well‑being of my kid and lead by example.
" The conversation with the therapists highlighted the broader issue of male emotional expression, with Williamson pointing out that societal expectations often label men as "feelingless," a perception that contributes to mental‑health struggles. She praised Green as an exemplary father and encouraged him to view his current emotional work as a necessary step toward personal growth. Green responded that he is still "firefighting" but aims to move beyond mere survival toward thriving.
The pair's son, Slimane Ray, was born in March 2021 and has become the focal point of both parents' public statements, underscoring their joint dedication to his upbringing despite their romantic separation. The recent hospital visit, while distressing, also served as a reminder of the everyday challenges that co‑parents navigate, and it has sparked a wave of support from fans who admire Green's willingness to share his vulnerabilities on a national platform
